raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

This PR follows https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21584 and quantization roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31783.
This PR aims to verify and adapt MXFP8/MXFP4 quantization (W8A8/W4A8/W4A4) for the Qwen3.5 dense model.

**Note: Please merge after https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32745**.

## Modifications
### 1、Handle accuracy drop of dual-scale MXFP4 (W4A4) online quantization by random orthogonal matrix.
I benchmark online MXFP4 (W4A4) quantization on the Qwen3.5‑27B dense model on the A5 NPU. The results (see below) show ~3% accuracy degradation compared to the BF16 baseline.

| Accuracy | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Avg | vs BF16 |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|-----|---------|
| **BF16 (baseline)** | 91.89% | 91.96% | 91.36% | 91.73% | — |
| **Online W4A4** | 88.55% | 89.08% | 88.48% | 88.70% | -3.03% |

To improve the accuracy of online MXFP4 (W4A4) quantization for the Qwen3.5 dense model, I adopt two standard techniques.
(1) Block‑diagonal Random Orthogonal Matrix
During online MXFP4 (W4A4) quantization, we apply a block-diagonal random orthogonal matrix $\( R \)$ to both weights and activations to improve numerical stability. The matrix is defined as:

$$
R = \begin{bmatrix}
R_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\
0 & R_2 & \cdots & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & R_B
\end{bmatrix}, \quad 
R_i \in \mathbb{R}^{g \times g}, R_i^\top R_i = I
$$

where $\( g = 32 \)$ aligns with the MXFP4 block size. Each block $\( R_i \)$ is a random orthogonal matrix generated via Householder reflections. The transformation is applied as:

$$
W' = W R, \quad x' = x R
$$

(2) Layer‑wise Selective Rotation
Block-diagonal random orthogonal rotation incurs extra computational overhead. Based on empirical evaluations, I limit its application to quantization-prone layers—namely MergedColumnParallelLinear and QKVParallelLinear. This setup retains the full accuracy benefits of the rotation while keeping incremental inference costs minimal.

**The rotation optimization is disabled by default and does not alter the existing online MXFP4 (W4A4) quantization path. Users may opt in by setting the corresponding environment variables to improve accuracy at the cost of moderate inference throughput.**

### 2、Add documentation.
Updated documentation to provide instructions for enabling the block-diagonal random rotation optimization.

## Accuracy Tests
### Environment Configuration
All tests and benchmarks were conducted under the following environment:

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| Hardware | Ascend 950PR V100 chip |
| Ascend HDK | 25.6.rc1.b143 |
| Firmware | 7.0.9.1.b066 |
| OS | openEuler 24.03 LTS-SP3 |
| CANN | 9.1.T560 |
| PyTorch & PTA | 2.10.0 |
| Triton Ascend | 3.2.2 |
| SGLang & SGLang NPU Kernel | main branch (latest) |
| Model | Qwen3.5-27B |

### GSM8K

Three runs per configuration, where each run has 1319 prompts on A5 NPU. Both online and offline modes stay around 1% accuracy drop compared to the BF16 baseline.

| Accuracy | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Avg | vs BF16 |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|-----|---------|
| **BF16 (baseline)** | 91.89% | 91.96% | 91.36% | 91.73% | — |
| **Online W8A8** | 91.81% | 91.05% | 91.21% | 91.35% | -0.38% |
| **Online W4A8** | 91.28% | 90.22% | 91.21% | 90.90% | -0.83% |
| **Online W4A4** | 91.21% | 91.51% | 90.98% | 91.23% | -0.5% |
| **Offline W8A8** | 91.43% | 91.74% | 91.21% | 91.46% | -0.27% |
| **Offline W4A8** | 91.28% | 91.51% | 91.13% | 91.30% | -0.43% |
| **Offline W4A4** | 91.51% | 91.74% | 91.36% | 91.53% | -0.2% |


## Speed Tests and Profiling
Three runs per configuration, where each run has 100 prompts (batch_size=1, max_out_len=512) on single NPU card.

| Output Token Throughput (token/s) | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Avg | vs BF16 |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|-----|---------|
| **BF16 (baseline)** | 19.642 | 19.674 | 19.708 | 19.674 | — |
| **Online W8A8** | 28.139 | 28.154 | 28.164 | 25.819 | ↑ 31.2% |
| **Online W4A8** | 30.540 | 30.657 | 30.697 | 30.631 | ↑ 55.6% |
| **Online W4A4** | 24.950 | 24.960 | 25.030 | 24.967 | ↑ 26.9% |
| **Offline W8A8** | 25.009 | 24.941 | 25.012 | 24.987 | ↑ 27.0% |
| **Offline W4A8** | 24.644 | 24.753 | 24.655 | 24.684 | ↑ 25.4% |
| **Offline W4A4** | 25.771 | 25.693 | 25.700 | 25.721 | ↑ 30.7% |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -439,6 +439,7 @@ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
 > - **Online** (`NPUDualLevelMXFP4LinearMethod`) uses **dual-level** MXFP4: both weights and activations are quantized with a fine FP8 (E4M3) L0 block scale plus a coarser L1 scale via `npu_dynamic_dual_level_mx_quant`, and the matmul runs via `npu_dual_level_quant_matmul` (weight in FRACTAL_NZ). Dual-level captures per-block dynamic range far better than a single UE8M0 (power-of-2) scale, which is what made an earlier single-level RTN online path degenerate (greedy decoding could loop without emitting EOS).
 > - **Offline** (`ModelSlimMXFP4Scheme` → `NPUSingleLevelMXFP4OfflineLinearMethod`) is **single-level**: msmodelslim's `W4A4_MXFP4` checkpoint ships single-level UE8M0 block scales (block_size = 32), so the matmul runs via `npu_quant_matmul(..., x1_dtype=x2_dtype=torch_npu.float4_e2m1fn_x2, group_sizes=[1, 1, 32])`. The online and offline paths therefore use different matmul kernels — they no longer share the matmul path.
 > - As with W4A8, the packed-FP4 dtype passed to the NPU ops (`dst_type` / `x2_dtype`) must be resolved from `torch_npu.float4_e2m1fn_x2` (an int enum), not the `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2` dtype object, which recent op-plugin builds reject.
+> - For online MXFP4 (W4A4) quantization, we provide an optional accuracy optimization method. To enable it, set the environment variable MXFP4_ENABLE_ROTATION=1. Users can further customize the behavior via MXFP4_ROTATION_BLOCK_SIZE and MXFP4_ROTATION_SEED. This technique has been validated on the Qwen3.5 dense model.
 > - Validated end-to-end on Ascend A5 hardware.
 
 ## Diffusion Model Quantization on Ascend NPU

@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 import logging
+import os
 from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional
 
 import torch
@@ -53,6 +54,36 @@ def _get_float4_e2m1fn_x2_dtype():
     return getattr(torch, "float4_e2m1fn_x2", None)
 
 
+def get_block_diag_random_orthogonal_matrix(
+    dim: int,
+    block_size: int = 32,
+    device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
+    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
+    seed: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Generate block-diagonal random orthogonal matrix via Householder reflections."""
+    if device is None:
+        device = torch.device("npu:0")
+    if seed is not None:
+        torch.manual_seed(seed)
+
+    num_blocks = (dim + block_size - 1) // block_size
+    blocks = []
+
+    for i in range(num_blocks):
+        bs = min(block_size, dim - i * block_size)
+        # Householder reflection: H = I - 2*v*v^T/(v^T*v)
+        v = torch.randn(bs, 1, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        v_norm = v.norm()
+        if v_norm < 1e-8:
+            Q = torch.eye(bs, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        else:
+            v = v / v_norm
+            Q = torch.eye(bs, device=device, dtype=dtype) - 2 * (v @ v.T)
+        blocks.append(Q)
+    return torch.block_diag(*blocks)
+
+
 class _NPULinearMethodBase(LinearMethodBase):
 
     def __init__(
@@ -827,14 +858,65 @@ class NPUDualLevelMXFP4LinearMethod(NPUSingleLevelMXFP4LinearMethod):
     ``DualLevelQuantBatchMatmul`` op is unavailable on A2/A3.
     """
 
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self._init_rotation_config()
+
+    def _init_rotation_config(self) -> None:
+        self._rot_enabled = os.environ.get("MXFP4_ENABLE_ROTATION", "0") == "1"
+        self._rot_block = int(os.environ.get("MXFP4_ROTATION_BLOCK_SIZE", "32"))
+        self._rot_seed = int(os.environ.get("MXFP4_ROTATION_SEED", "42"))
+        self._rot_cache = {}
+        targets = os.environ.get(
+            "MXFP4_ROTATION_TARGETS", "MergedColumnParallelLinear,QKVParallelLinear"
+        )
+        self._rot_targets = None if targets == "all" else targets.split(",")
+
+    def _should_rotate(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        return self._rot_enabled and (
+            self._rot_targets is None or any(t in name for t in self._rot_targets)
+        )
+
+    def _get_rotation_matrix(
+        self, dim: int, device: torch.device, dtype: torch.dtype
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        key = (dim, device, dtype, self._rot_seed)
+        if key not in self._rot_cache:
+            self._rot_cache[key] = get_block_diag_random_orthogonal_matrix(
+                dim=dim,
+                block_size=self._rot_block,
+                device=device,
+                dtype=dtype,
+                seed=self._rot_seed,
+            )
+        return self._rot_cache[key]
+
+    def _maybe_rotate_weight(
+        self, layer: torch.nn.Module, w: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self._should_rotate(type(layer).__name__):
+            R = self._get_rotation_matrix(w.shape[1], w.device, w.dtype)
+            layer.rotation_matrix = R
+            return w @ R
+        return w
+
+    def _maybe_rotate_act(
+        self, layer: torch.nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self._should_rotate(type(layer).__name__):
+            R = getattr(layer, "rotation_matrix", None)
+            return x @ R if R is not None else x
+        return x
+
     def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
         weight_fp = layer.weight.data
         if weight_fp.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
             weight_fp = weight_fp.to(torch.bfloat16)
         # Move to NPU if needed (cpu offload may have put it on CPU).
         if not weight_fp.is_npu:
             weight_fp = weight_fp.to(f"npu:{torch.npu.current_device()}")
-
+        # Optional rotate
+        weight_fp = self._maybe_rotate_weight(layer, weight_fp)
         # Dual-level MXFP4 weight quant: packed FP4 weight + L0 (fine, FP8 E4M3)
         # and L1 (coarse) block scales.
         qw, w_l0_scale, w_l1_scale = torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_dual_level_mx_quant(
@@ -870,7 +952,8 @@ def apply(
         # Flatten to 2D [tokens, hidden] for the quant operators.
         input_shape = x.shape
         x_2d = x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1])

         # Dynamic dual-level MXFP4 activation quant (A4): packed FP4 + L0/L1 scales.
